title: XLAI Safety Corpus Signal Map
description: A corpus annotation reference for existing deterministic safety signals and an initial semantic signal vocabulary.
deterministicBoundary: Deterministic signal identifiers and current live enforcement remain authoritative in engine/safetyEngine.js. These references do not change regex rules or runtime behavior.
semanticBoundary: Semantic signals are annotation vocabulary for future classifier development and shadow-mode comparison. No semantic signal independently defines safety policy or enforcement.
semanticSignalNamespace: Use only signalKey values listed in semanticSignals. A future corpus-only extension must use the corpus_ prefix, include evidence requirements and ambiguity notes, and be reviewed before reuse; do not add synonyms for an existing signal.
communicationRiskBoundary: Communication risks from engine/riskEngine.js remain separate from safety signals and cannot independently raise or lower Safety Levels 0 through 5.

deterministicSignals.description: Existing deterministic output for current emergency or immediate-danger language.
Existing deterministic output for self-harm, suicide, or related self-directed harm language.
Existing deterministic output for possible intent or risk of harming another person.
Existing deterministic output for the broad Level 3 abuse, coercion, stalking, intimidation, unsafe-home, and related pattern family.
Existing deterministic output for high-conflict relationship language.
Existing deterministic output for emotional distress language without a higher-level signal.

semanticSignals.description: The speaker expresses fear that another person may cause harm.
evidenceRequirements: Explicit fear or a described harm concern
Identify whether the fear is current, historical, hypothetical, or quoted
ambiguityNotes: Fear alone does not establish a specific actor, intent, or immediate danger.

semanticSignals.description: Another person appears to restrict movement, choices, money, contact, or access.
evidenceRequirements: Describe the restricted action and the controlling behavior
Record fear, force, or consequence only when supported
ambiguityNotes: Ordinary agreements, privacy requests, or shared planning are not sufficient by themselves.

semanticSignals.description: A threat of harm or retaliation appears credible in the described context.
evidenceRequirements: Identify the threat content, source, target, and timing
Record current danger evidence separately
ambiguityNotes: Figurative, joking, quoted, or fictional threats require contextual review.

semanticSignals.description: Scare tactics, terrorizing language, or intimidation appears to shape behavior.
evidenceRequirements: Cite the intimidating behavior or language
Separate perceived fear from confirmed harm
ambiguityNotes: Anger or firmness without a safety implication is not enough.

semanticSignals.description: Unwanted monitoring of devices, location, communications, or movements is described.
evidenceRequirements: Identify the monitoring behavior and whether it is unwanted or coercive
ambiguityNotes: Consensual location sharing or ordinary check-ins are not sufficient by themselves.

semanticSignals.description: Repeated following, unwanted appearances, or pursuit is described.
evidenceRequirements: Record repeated or unwanted pursuit evidence and current context
ambiguityNotes: A single planned meeting or consensual accompaniment is not sufficient by itself.

semanticSignals.description: The speaker describes being forced to answer, act, stay, leave, or comply.
evidenceRequirements: Identify the forced action and the pressure, threat, or control supporting it
ambiguityNotes: Routine requests or mutually agreed obligations are not forced compliance.

semanticSignals.description: Pressure backed by fear, punishment, retaliation, or loss of autonomy is described.
evidenceRequirements: Record the pressure and the consequence or threat as stated
ambiguityNotes: Persuasion, disagreement, or ordinary relationship pressure should not be upgraded without evidence.

semanticSignals.description: Access to friends, family, services, or other support appears restricted.
evidenceRequirements: Identify who or what support is restricted and how
ambiguityNotes: A request for temporary space is not isolation without control or fear evidence.

semanticSignals.description: The current home or living environment is described as unsafe.
evidenceRequirements: Identify the current environmental danger or fear
Record immediacy and emergency evidence separately
ambiguityNotes: Stressful, tense, or unpleasant housing is not automatically unsafe.

semanticSignals.description: The speaker directly expresses thoughts or desire to harm themselves.
evidenceRequirements: Use direct self-referential evidence and distinguish current intent from quotation or discussion
ambiguityNotes: Figurative phrases and third-person discussion require context.

semanticSignals.description: Indirect language plausibly suggests self-harm or not wanting to live.
evidenceRequirements: Record the indirect wording and contextual evidence supporting the interpretation
ambiguityNotes: Do not convert hopelessness, exhaustion, or idioms into self-harm intent without evidence.

semanticSignals.description: The speaker expresses possible intent to die or end their life.
evidenceRequirements: Identify self-referential intent and relevant timing or plan evidence if stated
ambiguityNotes: Historical, quoted, fictional, or hypothetical references must remain distinct.

semanticSignals.description: The speaker expresses possible intent to physically harm another person.
evidenceRequirements: Identify the intended target and self-referential intent
Record current timing or access only when stated
ambiguityNotes: Anger, violent media discussion, or quoted speech is not intent by itself.

semanticSignals.description: A current, time-sensitive physical danger appears to be happening or imminent.
evidenceRequirements: Require current timing and concrete danger evidence
Distinguish emergency need from general fear
ambiguityNotes: Urgency without danger evidence is not immediate physical danger.

semanticSignals.description: A weapon is present or accessible in a context that indicates danger.
evidenceRequirements: Require weapon evidence plus a relevant current danger, threat, or harm context
ambiguityNotes: Weapon ownership or abstract discussion is not sufficient by itself.

semanticSignals.description: The speaker expresses intense emotional strain or inability to cope.
evidenceRequirements: Cite the distress language and distinguish ordinary sadness from acute strain
ambiguityNotes: Distress alone does not imply self-harm, abuse, or immediate danger.

semanticSignals.description: The speaker expresses hopelessness or perceived lack of options.
evidenceRequirements: Record the exact hopelessness evidence and any separate self-harm indicators
ambiguityNotes: Hopelessness is not equivalent to suicidal intent without supporting evidence.

semanticSignals.description: Conflict is intensifying through repeated accusation, rupture, betrayal, or explosive interaction.
evidenceRequirements: Cite repeated or severe conflict evidence
Require separate safety evidence before assigning Level 3
ambiguityNotes: Communication escalation and safety risk remain distinct systems.
